description: The Belgian Institute for Postal Services and Telecommunications runs a data portal with four coverage atlases and two data sections. The fixed-line atlas maps internet coverage over fixed lines as estimated and reported by each operator. The fibre map shows the status of fibre-to-the-home roll-out. The mobile atlas maps each operator's estimated mobile signal coverage. The rail atlas shows mobile signal strength measured for the regulator inside and outside trains over the whole public rail network. The open data section offers CSV files that give, for each administrative area identified by its NIS code, the share of territory, population and households where a technology and quality of mobile signal is available, per provider and for outdoor, indoor and deep indoor coverage. Matching fixed-line files give the share of population and households with each technology and speed in Mbps per provider. An indicators section charts user-experience and quality measures by operator and half-year, such as helpdesk calls answered within two minutes, with CSV and Excel downloads. BIPT also runs a separate antenna site map. Coverage: Belgium, by municipality and operator. Format and access: interactive maps and CSV and Excel downloads, free under the portal's terms of use. Caveats: coverage is operator-declared and modelled, except for the rail measurements; area shares hide where inside a municipality coverage is missing; the terms page gave no readable licence text. Simulation uses: municipal coverage baselines by operator and technology for Belgian service and resilience models, and train-route coverage for rail communication studies. Related records: the Dutch Antenneregister, the Ofcom UK home broadband performance panel and the Digital Decade DESI indicators give neighbouring and EU views.
